relationships.name: James Glasgow II
relationships.basis: The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. John’s place in the brother group is additionally inferential.
relationships.limitations: Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.
relationships.record_scope: Existing father-profile propositions only: Robert-12 85% → 35%; Arthur-649 and Joseph-1543 each 82% → 35%; John-4027 76% → 30%; Mary-4030 64% → 22%. All five were probable; the first four are now possible and Mary uncertain. James-1024 remains the selected named candidate; no attachment is removed. The separate Irish-family review on24October subsequently assesses James-1024’s father78% and Samuel-1492’s father76%; the American father grades here are unchanged.

assessment_history.source_basis: Assess James of Moneymore, Glasgow-1024, as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

relationships.name: Joseph Glasgow
relationships.basis: Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. Glasgow-4028 and Glasgow-4029 are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.
relationships.limitations: The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The older James-1025 father of James-1024 remains 18%; no Scottish migration, Mary Harkness maternity, new mother, identity merge or live edit follows. Exact percentages express individual subjective judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied independent probabilities.

Glasgow-4028 and Glasgow-4029 are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

claims.limitations: The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The older James-1025 father of James-1024 remains 18%; no Scottish migration, Mary Harkness maternity, new mother, identity merge or live edit follows. Exact percentages express individual subjective judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied independent probabilities.

claims.reason: The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. John’s place in the brother group is additionally inferential. Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.

prior_assessment.source_basis: Assess James of Moneymore, Glasgow-1024, as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.
